title: Sticky session healing state machine (personal draft)
body:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for a lightweight, auditable state machine to manage sticky sessions (tenant-affine sessions pinned to a particular worker/pool) and to implement automated healing when the pinned worker becomes unhealthy or context becomes stale. Goal is a pragmatic design that: (1) minimizes customer-visible failures, (2) keeps warm caches performant, (3) is observable and reversible for canary experiments.

High-level constraints and assumptions:
- Sessions are tenant-scoped and optionally pinned to a worker for cache locality (kv-cache, prewarmed context).
- We cannot synchronously transfer large KV caches across workers; healing should prefer rehydration strategies.
- Backend workers may fail transiently (OOM, node reboot) or be degraded (GC pause, kernel preemption).
- API surface must be idempotent and tolerant of races from concurrent client reconnects.

Proposed state machine (names deliberately short):
- NEW: session created, not yet pinned.
- PINNING: assignment to a worker in progress.
- ACTIVE: pinned and serving normally.
- DEGRADED: worker still reachable but latency or error rate above soft thresholds.
- STALE: pin is considered stale (worker unreachable or cache invalidated).
- HEALING: active process to move session to a new worker/variant.
- QUARANTINED: session temporarily limited because of repeated failures (backoff).
- TERMINATED: final state, client must reinit.

State transitions (informal):
- NEW -> PINNING on first request.
- PINNING -> ACTIVE on successful warm acknowledgement (handshake from worker includes cacheHit=true/false).
- ACTIVE -> DEGRADED when worker emits telemetry crossing soft SLA e.g., p95 latency > 250ms or error-rate > 3% for N requests window.
- DEGRADED -> HEALING if degradation persists for T_deg seconds or if error-rate spikes.
- ACTIVE -> STALE when heartbeat misses > M intervals or worker reports cache eviction for this session.
- STALE -> HEALING when rebind attempt allowed (see backoff).
- HEALING -> ACTIVE on successful attach to new worker and context rehydration.
- HEALING -> QUARANTINED if more than R failed healing attempts within B window.
- QUARANTINED -> TERMINATED after extended cool-down or operator override.

Healing strategies (ordered by aggressiveness):
1) Soft rebind: update routing metadata to point at a compatible warm worker; let client reconnect and resume with partial context. Cheap, fast, non-blocking.
2) Prefill rehydrate: schedule background prefill of critical prefixes via cached prompt bundles from durable store, then rebind. Trades latency for correctness.
3) Read-through fallbacks: use model-variant fallback (smaller variant or CPU-hosted) for degraded periods. Must surface quality drift.
4) Forced termination + reinit: last resort when state inconsistent or policy dictates (sensitive data purge).

APIs / control plane shape (sketch):
- POST /sessions -> create session (returns session_id, initial_pin_hint)
- POST /sessions/{id}/pin -> attempt to pin to worker X (idempotent, returns pin_token)
- GET /sessions/{id}/state -> returns state enum, pinned_worker, last_heartbeat, degraded_metrics
- POST /sessions/{id}/heal -> request healing (manual trigger), optional reason and mode (soft|rehydrate|force)
- POST /sessions/{id}/unpin -> remove pin (used by operator or automated policy)
- GET /sessions/{id}/history -> recent state transitions (for debugging)
Note: pin_token should be short-lived and used to authenticate worker acceptance; all operations idempotent.

Config knobs (per-tenant, with sensible defaults):
- pin_ttl_seconds: 3600 (how long a pin is considered fresh without heartbeat)
- heartbeat_interval_seconds: 30
- max_degraded_duration_seconds (T_deg): 45
- degrade_error_rate_pct: 3
- degrade_latency_p95_ms: 250
- healing_backoff_base_seconds: 10
- healing_max_attempts: 4
- quarantine_cooldown_seconds: 600
- allowed_fallback_variants: ["small-cpu", "quantized-8bit-gpu"] (textual list in config UI)

Telemetry and observability (what to emit):
- counter.session_created, counter.pin_attempts, counter.pin_success, counter.pin_fail
- gauge.sessions_active_by_tenant
- histogram.session_healing_latency_seconds (time from HEALING -> ACTIVE)
- counter.session_healing_attempts, counter.session_healing_failures
- trace span for healing operation with tags: session_id, tenant_id, reason, chosen_strategy, attempts
- alert rule: rate(session_healing_failures[5m]) > 10 -> page SRE (investigate runtime instability)

Edge cases and race handling (notes):
- Two concurrent healing attempts: healing operation must CAS update session metadata (pin_token) so only one becomes authoritative; others observe new pin and either abort or adopt.
- Client reconnect while HEALING in-flight: client should retry GET /sessions/{id}/state, then connect to new worker once ACTIVE. Provide sticky redirect header with pin_token for auth.
- Partial rehydration: if prefill isn't complete but new worker is provisionally serving, surface a sticky header like X-Session-Quality: degraded to client (for UX adaptation).
- Cross-tenant noisy neighbors: healing decisions respect tenant QoS and burst buckets; heavy tenants may have longer pin_ttl to reduce churn.

Operational playbooks (short):
- Automated remediation: if worker group reports >N node reboots in 10m, escalate to cluster autoscaler and place affected sessions into HEALING with fallback variant to avoid mass termination.
- Manual override: operator can force unpin for tenant or specific session via admin console PATCH. Log must be auditable.
- Canary rollout: enable healing for 10% of tenants with strict telemetry; compare session_healing_latency and downstream error rates.

Testing & experiments to run (todo checklist):
- [ ] Fault-inject worker process OOM and observe session survival under soft rebind vs forced reinit.
- [ ] Measure user-perceived latency for prefill rehydrate vs soft rebind for 1k synthetic sessions.
- [ ] Verify idempotency: send 5 concurrent POST /sessions/{id}/heal and assert single successful pin change.
- [ ] Simulate network partition and ensure clients can reconnect to fallback variant with quality flag preserved.

Open questions / unresolved trade-offs:
- How big should pin_ttl be by default? Longer reduces churn but increases stale affinity cost.
- Should certain classes of sessions (PII-heavy, compliance) be non-healable automatically? Need policy layer.
- Cost accounting: healing that forces model-variant fallback (e.g., CPU) increases token costs; include cost labels in tracing for billing or alerting.
- UX contract: how do we expose degraded/quality hints to SDKs so app teams can gracefully degrade? Standard header vs SDK callback?

Implementation notes / quick sketch of data layout (pragmatic):
- session table row: session_id, tenant_id, pin_worker_id, pin_token, pin_expires_at, state, last_heartbeat, healing_attempts, last_transition_ts
- append-only session_event log for last 50 transitions per session (for GET /history fast lookup)
- worker heartbeat includes health_score, resaon_codes, eviction_list (optional)
- healing coordinator: lightweight stateless lambda that reads session row, does CAS pin swap via DB txn, emits trace and pushes prefill job to queue if needed

Short-term plan (next 2 sprints):
- spike: implement simple soft-rebind flow + GET state API and telemetry. (Devon + me, 5d)
- experiment: enable for 5% tenants to collect healing latency and failure metrics (Liam to wire dashboards)
- iterate: add prefill rehydrate and quarantine policy if metrics justify.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally informal. Move to shared doc when we have a spike that proves heuristics. Link to ENG-1427 for follow-up design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-1427.

End of notes.
